scenario: AITA for not wanting to be friends with my group anymore? | So I just finished my freshman year in college, and I found myself a pretty good friend group. I’ve always been really shy so the fact that I‘m part of a group means a lot to me. However, I’m the only one (in a group of 8) that is not in our school’s Honors College. Many people, including them, have assured me that this doesn’t mean they’re smarter than me or harder working than me, and I’ve accepted that. However, Honors College people all have some required courses to take that are just for them, so they all have classes together without me. And sometimes when we hang out, everyone talks about their classes and I feel completely left out. In addition, I found out that next year, they’re all living in the Honors College dorm building together. I can’t live there since I’m not in Honors College and I already feel left out enough. Now that they’ll all live together, it’s even more likely they’ll end up hanging out without me just because they’re all living together and just happen to run into each other and how can I blame them for that?? I have tried to talk to a couple of them about it and one in particular said that I have no right to make them feel bad for being happy that they can live together but I feel like if they had an ounce of empathy, they’d realize that 7 people of an 8 person group living together is rather unfair. I don’t want to have to start over and find new friends but I also feel like I deserve friends who will try to include me. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to feel this way about my friends. Let me start by understanding the situation better. I just finished my freshman year in college, and I've managed to find a pretty good friend group. Considering I've always been really shy, being part of a group means a lot to me. But here's the thing: I'm the only one in a group of eight who isn't in our school's Honors College. Now, people, including my friends, have told me that this doesn't mean they're smarter or harder working than me, and I've tried to accept that. However, the Honors College students have some required courses that are just for them, so they all have classes together without me. That's already a bit tough because when we hang out, everyone talks about their classes, and I feel completely left out. To make things worse, I found out that next year, they're all living in the Honors College dorm building together. I can't live there since I'm not in the Honors College, and I already feel left out enough. Now that they'll all live together, it's even more likely they'll end up hanging out without me just because they're all living together and happen to run into each other. I can't blame them for that, can I? I've tried talking to a couple of them about it, and one person in particular said that I have no right to make them feel bad for being happy that they can live together. But I feel like if they had an ounce of empathy, they'd realize that seven people of an eight-person group living together is rather unfair. I don't want to have to start over and find new friends, but I also feel like I deserve friends who will try to include me. So, is it AITA (Ask aITA) to feel this way? Am I overreacting, or is this a valid concern? I need to figure out whether my feelings are justified or if I'm being too sensitive. First, I need to understand what AITA means. From what I gather, AITA is a term used to ask if someone is being too hard on themselves or if their feelings are justified in a particular situation. So, in this context, I'm asking if it's AITA for me to feel upset about my friends moving into a dorm together and potentially excluding me. Now, let's break down the situation. I'm feeling left out because my friends are all in the Honors College, taking different classes, and now living together. This makes it harder for us to spend time together outside of class. I tried talking to them about it, and one of them responded by saying I shouldn't make them feel bad for being happy about living together. On one hand, I can see their perspective. They're excited about living together and having more time to hang out. On the other hand, I feel like I'm being excluded because I'm not part of the Honors College, and this is affecting our friendship. I wonder if it's fair to expect them to make an effort to include me when they're living together. Is it reasonable to ask them to make time for me, or should I accept that our friendship might change because of these circumstances? Also, I'm considering whether I'm being too sensitive. Maybe it's normal for friendships to shift when people have different schedules or living arrangements. But at the same time, I feel like I deserve friends who value our friendship enough to make an effort to include me. I'm also thinking about whether there's a middle ground. Maybe I can find new friends who are in a similar situation as me, or perhaps I can talk to my friends about setting aside specific times to hang out despite their living arrangements. Another thing to consider is whether I'm projecting my feelings onto them. Maybe they don't actually intend to exclude me, but I'm interpreting their actions in a way that makes me feel left out. It's possible that they're just as excited about living together as I am about staying in touch, but communication is key here. I also need to reflect on whether I'm being realistic in expecting them to include me in the same way as before. If they're all living together, it's natural for them to spend more time with each other, especially since they're already a close-knit group. In summary, I'm feeling a mix of emotions: sadness about potentially losing a close friend group, frustration at feeling excluded, and uncertainty about whether my feelings are justified or if I'm being too sensitive. I need to find a way to balance my emotions with the reality of the situation and decide how to move forward in a way that respects both my feelings and the dynamics of the friendship. Maybe I should consider talking to them again, expressing my feelings without making them feel guilty, and seeing if we can find a compromise or a way to maintain our friendship despite the changes. Alternatively, I might need to accept that our friendship will change and look for new friends who are in a similar situation as me. Ultimately, I want to make sure that I'm not holding onto a friendship that's no longer fulfilling for me, but I also don't want to give up on a group that means a lot to me without giving it a fair chance. It's a tough situation, and I'm not sure what the best approach is. I think the key here is communication. If I can express my feelings openly and honestly, without blaming them, maybe we can find a way to navigate this together. If not, then I might need to consider whether this friendship is still right for me and explore other options for building connections in college. In the end, I believe that my feelings are valid, and it's important to prioritize my emotional well-being. Whether that means finding new friends or working through this with my current group, I need to make the choice that feels right for me.
